articles.title: FX option expiries for 19 October 10am New York cut
articles.description: There is just one key expiry level to take note of on the day, as highlighted in bold below. That being for EUR/USD at the 1.1200 level, with the strike holding roughly 30 pips from the spot price. The expiries here could offer some attraction if price action starts drifting lower during the session ahead, and that could anchor price action around 1.1200 going into the cut. Having said that, the broader market direction will still be dictated primarily by Treasury yields and dollar sentiment for the most part. As such, it is unlikely that expiries would be able to drive a sustained move on its own. Besides that, there isn't much else on the board for today but there will be a big one to watch for EUR/USD at the 1.1265 level. The expiries there are currently already sizable, with €4.1 billion interest sitting at the level. So, that could make the 1.1265 mark a focal point heading into tomorrow's cut. But again, we will first have to see how price action plays out today and that will likely depend more on what happens in the bond market and dollar sentiment in general. For more information on how to use this data, you may refer to this post here and/or refer to the Q&A below. This article was written by Justin Low at investinglive.com.

articles.title: Asian shares are mixed as tech stocks remain volatile and oil falls
articles.description: Asian shares are mixed as the volatility in technology stocks persists. U.S. futures have edged higher ahead of another week of American corporate earnings. A sell-off of technology shares from Asia to Wall Street has recently put downward pressure on stock markets, as investor concerns grow over the sustainability of the artificial intelligence boom. Oil prices have declined more than 1% after President Donald Trump’s decision to waive sweeping sanctions on Russia, including on Russian energy. On Friday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 declined 1.1%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.3%, and the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite sank 2.1%.
